facts.label: Analysis by dimension
facts.text: Reported EBITDA overstates earnings power, so creditors should anchor on Segment Adjusted EBITDA. The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA; the figure derived here from income before tax, net finance costs and depreciation is USD 1,254 million over the last twelve months, USD 189 million above Segment Adjusted EBITDA, because it carries the non-cash metal price lag of USD 289 million, partly offset by USD 100 million of net other items. The lag is a timing gain that reverses when aluminium prices fall, and it was already negative in the third quarter of 2026, so net leverage of 1.32x on reported EBITDA is the favourable end of the range and 1.56x is the better guide. facts.text: Free cash flow is real but modest against EBITDA because working capital absorbs the rise in metal prices. Free Cash Flow was USD 223 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 68 million a year earlier and USD 333 million over the last twelve months, which is 0.27x reported EBITDA. Working capital absorbed USD 488 million in the nine months against USD 161 million a year earlier as inventories and receivables rose with metal prices, and capital expenditure net of inflows was USD 197 million. facts.label: Analysis by dimension

facts.label: Analysis by dimension
facts.text: Non-recourse factoring is a material source of funding outside debt that creditors should track. Receivables derecognized under factoring programs were USD 417 million at September 30, 2026, USD 430 million at year-end 2025 and USD 376 million at year-end 2024; the programs had combined limits of about USD 711 million, and their cost of USD 15 million in the nine months is excluded from Adjusted EBITDA. Pension and other benefit obligations of USD 341 million are a further claim outside debt. facts.label: Strongest contrary evidence
facts.text: The case for improving credit quality weakens if aluminium prices fall: the metal price lag would reverse and remove part of the USD 289 million that reported EBITDA carries, although working capital would then release some of the USD 488 million it absorbed in the first nine months of 2026. Shareholder returns also compete with deleveraging: a new buyback program of up to USD 300 million has USD 257 million remaining, and the issuer's target leverage range of 1.5x to 2.5x leaves room to add debt at 1.56x. The view would strengthen if net debt keeps falling while the lag stays flat, and would weaken if net leverage on Segment Adjusted EBITDA returned to the 2.19x of March 31, 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 41; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C23; calculation C40; calculation C47

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- The maturity ladder is drawn at December 31, 2025 because the quarterly reports print no maturity table; it does not reflect the July 28, 2026 redemption of USD 100 million of the 2028 notes or later currency movements on the euro notes, so the debt maturities chart overstates 2028 by that amount and the principal reconciliation covers year-end only. Severity: Low. Action: use the maturity table of the next annual report or an issuer schedule at September 30, 2026. - The senior notes are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries that the documents do not name, the indentures are not supplied, and the margins, reference rates and maturities of the credit facilities, finance leases and other loans are not stated, so the obligor scope and pricing of each facility in the debt stack and debt instruments tables are incomplete and no structural-priority view can be drawn. Finance lease liabilities of USD 27 million and other loans of USD 28 million are carried inside total debt but left out of the debt stack because no source states their legal rank, so the stack covers USD 1,762 million of USD 1,817 million. Severity: Low. Action: supply the indentures, the guarantor list and the lease and loan terms. - The October 22, 2026 amendment of the Pan-U.S. ABL falls after the balance sheet date and is excluded from September 30, 2026 debt and liquidity; the sources do not state availability, borrowing base, covenant terms or whether the springing maturity remains after the amendment, and the fixed charge coverage covenant level and letters of credit drawn on the facility are not stated at all, so liquidity after the amendment is not established, covenant headroom is not calculable and no pro forma figure is given. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the credit agreement and the text of the amendment. - Lines the statements print as a dash are carried as not supplied, not as zero: collection of deferred purchase price receivable (9M 2026), acquisition of subsidiaries (FY2025), proceeds from disposals (FY2024 and 9M 2025), other investing activities (FY2024 and 9M 2026), payment of financing costs (FY2025), proceeds from issuance of long-term debt (FY2025), impairment of assets (9M 2025), unrealized exchange gains (FY2025) and other adjustments (9M 2025); the nine-month statements also do not print proceeds from issuance of long-term debt, payment of financing costs or acquisition of subsidiaries. The sums hold when these are read as nil. Severity: Low. Action: confirm against the filed tables. - Some prior-period items are not in the sources: the balance sheet at September 30, 2025, so debt, cash and leverage at that date are not calculable and the nine-month 2025 column is omitted from the balance sheet; the face value of debt and the availability under the facilities at December 31, 2024, so the principal reconciliation and undrawn committed facilities for FY2024 are not supplied; receivables derecognized under factoring at September 30, 2025; and the issuer's stated leverage at year-end dates and at September 30, 2025. Severity: Low. Action: supply the September 30, 2025 quarterly report and the prior annual report. - Some items are not separately disclosed: maintenance against growth capital expenditure, so cash conversion before growth projects cannot be measured; interest income, which is inside finance costs - net, so net interest expense cannot be separated from the cash interest paid used for cover; and the carrying values of the euro senior notes, which the filings print in dollars only. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the dollar ratios shown; obtain management's capital expenditure split if conversion before growth is wanted. - The sources do not say whether the factoring programs are committed, and USD 417 million of receivables derecognized under them at September 30, 2026 sits outside net debt, so the funding risk from a withdrawal cannot be sized. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the program terms. - EBITDA (Reported) is not stated by the issuer and is derived from income before tax, net finance costs and depreciation and amortization; it carries the non-cash metal price lag of USD 289 million over the last twelve months and unrealized derivative results, so net leverage on it is 1.32x against 1.56x on Segment Adjusted EBITDA. Severity: Medium. This module shows both measures and anchors conclusions on Segment Adjusted EBITDA; no further action is needed. - Net debt at carrying value less cash differs from the issuer's net debt by USD 1 million at March 31, 2026 and September 30, 2026 because the issuer also deducts the fair value of cross currency basis swaps net of margin calls. Severity: Low. Both figures are shown; no further action is needed. - FY2024 Segment Adjusted EBITDA was revised in the annual report (Aerospace and Transportation from USD 285 million to USD 292 million, total from USD 568 million to USD 575 million, metal price lag from USD 55 million to USD 48 million); the revised amounts are used and both versions are logged. Severity: Low. No further action is needed.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: No sponsor or controlling shareholder appears in the supplied filings, so sponsor extraction, the usual leveraged-credit hazard, is not indicated, but the board alone decides shareholder returns. Four holders of record hold the shares, and one United States record holder acting through the registrar holds 93.77% of them, so beneficial owners cannot be identified; the annual report incorporates its beneficial-ownership table by reference to a proxy statement that was not supplied. A holder crossing 30% of capital or voting rights must offer for all shares under the articles, and the senior notes carry a repurchase offer at 101% on a change of control, although the indenture definition of a change of control is not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39, 48, 108–109, 126, 128–129; calculation C24

facts.label: Key findings

Packaging rolled products are 44.63% of FY2025 revenue, the packaging and automotive rolled segment is 59.97% of external revenue, and the two largest customers are 21.25% of revenue, with the ten largest around 56%. Management says the largest aerospace contracts run for several years and general industrial contracts for a year or less, so contract visibility is strongest in the segment with the highest margin, 17.23% in FY2025 against 6.95% for packaging and automotive sheet. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The 2026 earnings step-up mixes base-case and temporary drivers, which matters because buybacks are paid from it. Revenue rose 25.61% in 9M 2026 while shipments fell 0.88%, so growth came from revenue per tonne, which the company ties to higher metal prices, not from volume, and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,074 million includes a non-cash metal price lag of USD 222 million, or 20.67%. Management credits automotive sheet shortages in North America, favourable scrap and strong recycling, and says its 2028 targets of Adjusted EBITDA of USD 900 million and free cash flow of USD 300 million, both before metal price lag, leave out the scrap environment and the 2026 shortage benefit; the 2026 guidance of USD 1,030 million to USD 1,060 million is above that EBITDA target, and guidance was raised at each of the three 2026 reports. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Capital allocation favours shareholders inside a deleveraging track, a mixed pattern for creditors. Buybacks were USD 79 million in FY2024, USD 115 million in FY2025 and USD 78 million in 9M 2026, no dividend is paid, and a USD 300 million program runs to the end of 2028 with USD 257 million unused at September 30, 2026. In FY2024, with cash from operations of USD 301 million below net capital expenditure of USD 401 million, the company still repurchased shares and cash fell from USD 223 million to USD 141 million; in 9M 2026 free cash flow of USD 223 million covered buybacks 2.86x and the company repaid USD 106 million of long-term debt. The chief executive officer changed on January 1, 2026 through an internal succession, and the board extended the buyback authority in March 2026. The constraints are earnings that lean on one segment, working capital that absorbed USD 488 million in 9M 2026 and cash returned to shareholders. facts.text: Financial policy is the main controllable risk. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence that the credit is better than adequate is that the stress case stays inside the target range: if the packaging and automotive sheet margin returned to its FY2025 level, last-twelve-month Segment Adjusted EBITDA would fall by about USD 188 million to USD 877 million, net leverage would be 1.89x and cash interest cover 8.77x, with USD 992 million of liquidity and no note due before June 2028. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Constellium converts aluminium into specialty rolled and extruded products for aerospace, packaging, automotive and industrial customers, so its credit is that of a conversion business whose margin, not the metal price, drives cash flow. FY2025 revenue was USD 8,449 million across three segments, the group operated 23 manufacturing facilities at September 30, 2026, and the only portfolio changes in the period are a USD 3 million purchase of a controlling interest in 2024 and the 2026 disposal of a 54% interest for USD 2 million, so cash flow comes from operations, not from deals. Cash-flow visibility is strongest in aerospace, where the largest contracts are multi-year and the segment earned 17.23% in FY2025, and weakest in general industrial work, where contracts run a year or less. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: No sponsor or controlling shareholder appears in the supplied filings, so the board, not an owner, sets financial policy, and the parent is a French company listed on the NYSE whose US assets sit in a wholly owned US holding company. The senior notes are issued by the parent and guaranteed by unnamed subsidiaries, the asset-based facility is borrowed by three US operating companies and the inventory facility by two French ones, which layers the debt structure, and no dividend is paid while buybacks of USD 78 million were made in 9M 2026. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue growth in 2026 came from price, not volume, so revenue durability depends on conversion margins rather than on the metal price. Revenue rose 25.61% in 9M 2026 and revenue per tonne 26.73% while shipments fell 0.88%; aerospace and transportation shipments rose 19.48%, packaging and automotive sheet shipments fell 3.29% and automotive structures fell 2.58%. Prices are set at metal cost plus a conversion margin and customers face high switching costs from long qualification, which supports margins. Demand follows aircraft build rates and light vehicle production, which are cyclical, and beverage can demand, which the annual report calls relatively resilient in downturns and which is 44.63% of revenue through packaging rolled products; the United States takes 39.15% of revenue by destination and trade policy is a stated risk. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Margins are defended against metal prices by pass-through but remain exposed to volume, because the company says its capital-intensive operations generally have high fixed costs that it may not be able to cut quickly, and conversion costs are large against conversion revenue, although the filings give no fixed and variable split. Cost of metal is 63.11% of FY2025 revenue and passes through, production costs are 24.12% and other segment expenses 4.25%, so conversion costs take 76.90% of conversion revenue and, if every one were fixed, a 1% fall in conversion revenue would cut Segment Adjusted EBITDA by up to 4.33%. The same leverage worked upward in 9M 2026: conversion revenue rose 20.75% against production costs of 6.38%, lifting Segment Adjusted EBITDA 68.05%. A large part of energy needs is fixed-price, a majority of slabs are cast in-house, the ten largest metal suppliers supply about 49% of volumes, and the largest US labour agreements run to 2029 and 2030, which holds the cost base steady but limits flexibility if volumes fall. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 26, 56, 94, 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13

facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry and buyer power are the likely reasons margins are thinner in packaging and automotive sheet than in aerospace, where qualification barriers protect them. The industry is competitive on quality, price, delivery and innovation, the packaging and automotive sheet segment earned 6.95% on revenue in FY2025 against 17.23% in aerospace-led products, and the two largest customers are 21.25% of revenue, which gives them negotiating weight, although the filings do not say which segment they buy from. New entrants face heavy capital needs and long customer qualification, substitutes such as steel, glass, plastics and composites compete in some uses, and supplier power is limited because most slabs are cast in-house and the ten largest metal suppliers supply about 49% of volumes. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 12–13, 94; calculation C14; calculation C25

facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the credit is supported by an improved aerospace and defense environment, management guidance raised at each 2026 report, the asset-based facility extended to October 2031 and no note maturity before June 2028, while headwinds are a possible fading of the automotive sheet shortage and favourable scrap, a seasonally weak fourth quarter that guidance implies at USD 178 million to USD 208 million of Segment Adjusted EBITDA, and a metal price lag that reverses if prices fall. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 23–24; EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026-q1xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026-q2xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C20; calculation C33; calculation C8; calculation C29; calculation C28

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The primary downside is a normalisation of the packaging and automotive sheet margin that reaches creditors through leverage and refinancing, not through liquidity. The initiating condition is the end of the North American automotive sheet shortage and favourable scrap, which management says its 2028 targets exclude; the first operating break is a return of that segment's margin from 10.01% over the last twelve months to its FY2025 level of 6.95%, which removes about USD 188 million of Segment Adjusted EBITDA and takes it to USD 877 million. Net leverage would then be 1.89x and cash interest cover 8.77x, still inside the 1.5x to 2.5x range; a fall in metal prices would also turn the metal price lag negative in reported EBITDA but would release working capital, which absorbed USD 488 million in 9M 2026. Liquidity of USD 992 million and the absence of a note maturity before June 2028 mean that liquidity distress is not indicated; the board's levers are buybacks, which were USD 78 million in nine months, growth capital spending and factoring, and the observable trigger is fourth-quarter Segment Adjusted EBITDA below USD 178 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026-q1xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 38; calculation C17; calculation C19; calculation C5; calculation C9; calculation C20; calculation C7

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Constellium presents an adequate business profile supported by qualified aerospace and automotive franchises, metal pass-through and no sponsor, but credit quality is constrained by thin margins in packaging and automotive sheet, customer and segment concentration, and a policy that permits leverage up to 2.5x. Cash-flow durability appears adequate, because free cash flow covered buybacks 2.86x in 9M 2026 but is only 31.27% of Segment Adjusted EBITDA over the last twelve months. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the leverage held through 2027, quoted note prices and the asset-based facility, ahead of USD 1,066 million of notes due in 2028 and 2029. The primary downside path is a reversal of the packaging and automotive sheet margin. How the business profile compares with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established, and a more definitive opinion would need the legal terms of the debt, a peer set and the availability of the asset-based facility after the amendment. The top risk is a margin reversal in packaging and automotive sheet. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C19

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases are sufficient for the short credit snapshot of Constellium SE on audited FY2025 and unaudited Q3 2026 figures, but not for conclusions on guarantors, covenant headroom, ratings or market pricing. Creditors can rely on the reported debt, liquidity and earnings statements, while legal-document, agency and trading-level questions stay open until those documents are supplied.

Coverage runs without a break from the FY2025 annual report to the third-quarter report published on 2026-10-28, eight days before the cutoff. One event falls after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet: the October 22, 2026 amendment of the Pan-U.S. ABL facility, which raised commitments and extended maturity, and its effect on availability is not established. The financing terms come only from the notes to the filings, because no executed credit agreement, indenture, rating report or bond quote was supplied.

CONSTELLIUM SE (issuer id cstm), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. Scope: the financial foundation for the short credit snapshot: statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics for FY2024, FY2025 and the 2026 quarters to September 30, 2026.
## Sources

| EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026-q2xearningspressre.htm.jsonl | Earnings press release for the second quarter and first half of 2026, dated July 29, 2026 | 2026-07-29 | e63d9d2c8751c74a8e5dada7565bb132595b18bca9ad9c4ef12f98be9c09a4ae | H1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA, Segment Adjusted EBITDA, net debt and stated leverage |

| EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl | Earnings press release for the third quarter and nine months of 2026, dated October 28, 2026 | 2026-10-28 | 6f8f81f1120f3b29fefca592a7a8bc48697b73e3a95ba4114c430951126fc70a | 9M 2026 reconciliations, net debt, stated leverage, guidance, recent developments |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | Accepted output of the Source readiness module for this run | 2026-11-05 | 84cdf41c113f1349056f1d122dba5d9265bbff48d60d0eebe50f2c5819bfaed4 | Source inventory, entity and period coverage, gap register |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Constellium's leverage has fallen to 1.56x net debt to last-twelve-month Segment Adjusted EBITDA at September 30, 2026, from 2.53x at year-end 2025, and no senior note matures before 2028, so creditors face low near-term refinancing risk.

The improvement is real but flattered on reported measures: reported EBITDA of USD 1,254 million includes a non-cash metal price lag gain of USD 289 million over the last twelve months, so net leverage is 1.32x on that basis against 1.56x on the issuer's definition. Free Cash Flow of USD 333 million over the same period is only 0.27x reported EBITDA because working capital absorbed USD 488 million in the first nine months of 2026. Cash interest of USD 100 million is covered 12.54x by reported EBITDA and 10.65x by Segment Adjusted EBITDA. The October 22, 2026 amendment of the Pan-U.S. ABL falls after the balance sheet date and is not reflected in debt or liquidity.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 9, 15, 23; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; calculation C46; calculation C47; calculation C48; calculation C11; calculation C23; calculation C38; calculation C51; calculation C40; calculation C20; calculation C49; calculation C50
### Analysis by dimension

Leverage has fallen because earnings grew while net debt eased, and the issuer's own definition confirms the level. Net debt at carrying value, gross debt less cash, was USD 1,824 million at year-end 2025 and USD 1,659 million at September 30, 2026, a fall of USD 165 million, while Segment Adjusted EBITDA over the last twelve months rose from USD 720 million to USD 1,065 million on favourable price, mix and metal costs in packaging and automotive rolled products and higher aerospace volumes. That is 2.53x falling to 1.56x, and the issuer states 1.6x at September 30, 2026 on the same definition, with 2.2x at March 31, 2026 and 1.8x at June 30, 2026.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 9; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 4, 16; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026-q2xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026-q1xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; calculation C42; calculation C45; calculation C70; calculation C46; calculation C47

Reported EBITDA overstates earnings power, so creditors should anchor on Segment Adjusted EBITDA. The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA; the figure derived here from income before tax, net finance costs and depreciation is USD 1,254 million over the last twelve months, USD 189 million above Segment Adjusted EBITDA, because it carries the non-cash metal price lag of USD 289 million, partly offset by USD 100 million of net other items. The lag is a timing gain that reverses when aluminium prices fall, and it was already negative in the third quarter of 2026, so net leverage of 1.32x on reported EBITDA is the favourable end of the range and 1.56x is the better guide.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 6; calculation C11; calculation C17; calculation C23; calculation C69; calculation C78; calculation C79; calculation C48

Interest cover is ample and has improved mainly through earnings, because cash interest has barely moved. Cash interest paid over the last twelve months was USD 100 million against USD 104 million in FY2025, so cover rose from 8.14x to 12.54x on reported EBITDA and from 6.92x to 10.65x on Segment Adjusted EBITDA. Every senior note carries a fixed coupon and the Pan-U.S. ABL carried no drawing at September 30, 2026, so a rise in interest rates would not change cash interest until the notes are refinanced in 2028 and 2029.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 15; calculation C20; calculation C49; calculation C50

Free cash flow is real but modest against EBITDA because working capital absorbs the rise in metal prices. Free Cash Flow was USD 223 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 68 million a year earlier and USD 333 million over the last twelve months, which is 0.27x reported EBITDA. Working capital absorbed USD 488 million in the nine months against USD 161 million a year earlier as inventories and receivables rose with metal prices, and capital expenditure net of inflows was USD 197 million. Cash also funded buybacks of USD 78 million and debt repayment of USD 106 million, including the USD 100 million partial redemption of the 2028 notes, so gross debt fell USD 127 million and cash rose USD 38 million.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 39; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C37; calculation C36; calculation C38; calculation C51; calculation C40; calculation C39; calculation C32; calculation C80

Liquidity is adequate and the next principal maturities are distant. The issuer states total liquidity of USD 992 million at September 30, 2026: USD 158 million of cash, USD 541 million available under the Pan-U.S. ABL, USD 114 million under the French inventory facility and USD 179 million under factoring programs, so USD 655 million is undrawn committed lending. No senior note matures before June 2028, when USD 225 million remains after the July 2026 partial redemption, and the 2029 notes total USD 841 million, so the refinancing wall is USD 1,066 million across 2028 and 2029; the French facility, undrawn, expires in December 2027.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 108, 110; calculation C58; calculation C59; calculation C73; calculation C74; calculation C77

Non-recourse factoring is a material source of funding outside debt that creditors should track. Receivables derecognized under factoring programs were USD 417 million at September 30, 2026, USD 430 million at year-end 2025 and USD 376 million at year-end 2024; the programs had combined limits of about USD 711 million, and their cost of USD 15 million in the nine months is excluded from Adjusted EBITDA. If banks withdrew these programs the receivables would return to the balance sheet and have to be funded from cash, the ABL or new debt. Pension and other benefit obligations of USD 341 million are a further claim outside debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 38, 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation C71

Two subsequent events touch debt and are kept out of period figures. On July 28, 2026 the issuer redeemed USD 100 million of the USD 325 million 2028 notes, which is already in the September 30, 2026 balances. On October 22, 2026, after the balance sheet date, the Pan-U.S. ABL was amended to raise commitments from USD 550 million to USD 700 million and extend maturity to October 22, 2031; the sources state no draw or repayment, so no pro forma net debt is shown, and availability, borrowing base and covenant terms after the amendment are not established.

### Strongest contrary evidence

The case for improving credit quality weakens if aluminium prices fall: the metal price lag would reverse and remove part of the USD 289 million that reported EBITDA carries, although working capital would then release some of the USD 488 million it absorbed in the first nine months of 2026. Shareholder returns also compete with deleveraging: a new buyback program of up to USD 300 million has USD 257 million remaining, and the issuer's target leverage range of 1.5x to 2.5x leaves room to add debt at 1.56x. The view would strengthen if net debt keeps falling while the lag stays flat, and would weaken if net leverage on Segment Adjusted EBITDA returned to the 2.19x of March 31, 2026.

## Gaps

- The maturity ladder is drawn at December 31, 2025 because the quarterly reports print no maturity table; it does not reflect the July 28, 2026 redemption of USD 100 million of the 2028 notes or later currency movements on the euro notes, so the debt maturities chart overstates 2028 by that amount and the principal reconciliation covers year-end only. Severity: Low. Action: use the maturity table of the next annual report or an issuer schedule at September 30, 2026.

- The senior notes are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries that the documents do not name, the indentures are not supplied, and the margins, reference rates and maturities of the credit facilities, finance leases and other loans are not stated, so the obligor scope and pricing of each facility in the debt stack and debt instruments tables are incomplete and no structural-priority view can be drawn. Finance lease liabilities of USD 27 million and other loans of USD 28 million are carried inside total debt but left out of the debt stack because no source states their legal rank, so the stack covers USD 1,762 million of USD 1,817 million. Severity: Low. Action: supply the indentures, the guarantor list and the lease and loan terms.

- The October 22, 2026 amendment of the Pan-U.S. ABL falls after the balance sheet date and is excluded from September 30, 2026 debt and liquidity; the sources do not state availability, borrowing base, covenant terms or whether the springing maturity remains after the amendment, and the fixed charge coverage covenant level and letters of credit drawn on the facility are not stated at all, so liquidity after the amendment is not established, covenant headroom is not calculable and no pro forma figure is given. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the credit agreement and the text of the amendment.

- Lines the statements print as a dash are carried as not supplied, not as zero: collection of deferred purchase price receivable (9M 2026), acquisition of subsidiaries (FY2025), proceeds from disposals (FY2024 and 9M 2025), other investing activities (FY2024 and 9M 2026), payment of financing costs (FY2025), proceeds from issuance of long-term debt (FY2025), impairment of assets (9M 2025), unrealized exchange gains (FY2025) and other adjustments (9M 2025); the nine-month statements also do not print proceeds from issuance of long-term debt, payment of financing costs or acquisition of subsidiaries. The sums hold when these are read as nil. Severity: Low. Action: confirm against the filed tables.

- Some prior-period items are not in the sources: the balance sheet at September 30, 2025, so debt, cash and leverage at that date are not calculable and the nine-month 2025 column is omitted from the balance sheet; the face value of debt and the availability under the facilities at December 31, 2024, so the principal reconciliation and undrawn committed facilities for FY2024 are not supplied; receivables derecognized under factoring at September 30, 2025; and the issuer's stated leverage at year-end dates and at September 30, 2025. Severity: Low. Action: supply the September 30, 2025 quarterly report and the prior annual report.

- Some items are not separately disclosed: maintenance against growth capital expenditure, so cash conversion before growth projects cannot be measured; interest income, which is inside finance costs - net, so net interest expense cannot be separated from the cash interest paid used for cover; and the carrying values of the euro senior notes, which the filings print in dollars only. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the dollar ratios shown; obtain management's capital expenditure split if conversion before growth is wanted.

- The sources do not say whether the factoring programs are committed, and USD 417 million of receivables derecognized under them at September 30, 2026 sits outside net debt, so the funding risk from a withdrawal cannot be sized. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the program terms.

- EBITDA (Reported) is not stated by the issuer and is derived from income before tax, net finance costs and depreciation and amortization; it carries the non-cash metal price lag of USD 289 million over the last twelve months and unrealized derivative results, so net leverage on it is 1.32x against 1.56x on Segment Adjusted EBITDA. Severity: Medium. This module shows both measures and anchors conclusions on Segment Adjusted EBITDA; no further action is needed.

- Net debt at carrying value less cash differs from the issuer's net debt by USD 1 million at March 31, 2026 and September 30, 2026 because the issuer also deducts the fair value of cross currency basis swaps net of margin calls. Severity: Low. Both figures are shown; no further action is needed.

- FY2024 Segment Adjusted EBITDA was revised in the annual report (Aerospace and Transportation from USD 285 million to USD 292 million, total from USD 568 million to USD 575 million, metal price lag from USD 55 million to USD 48 million); the revised amounts are used and both versions are logged. Severity: Low. No further action is needed.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Constellium is an NYSE-listed French aluminium converter with no sponsor or controlling shareholder in the supplied filings, so creditors depend on board policy; governance risk is moderate, because buybacks and a 1.5x to 2.5x leverage target coexist with falling leverage and a debt paydown.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 38–40, 48, 126, 128–129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2

Management says metal cost is passed through to customers, so margin follows product mix and volume, but the business is concentrated: packaging rolled products are 44.63% of FY2025 revenue and the two largest customers 21.25%. In 9M 2026 free cash flow of USD 223 million covered buybacks of USD 78 million 2.86x, leverage was 1.6x, and the July 2026 redemption cut the 2028 notes to USD 225 million.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93, 97; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 15; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C14; calculation C19
### Key findings

No sponsor or controlling shareholder appears in the supplied filings, so sponsor extraction, the usual leveraged-credit hazard, is not indicated, but the board alone decides shareholder returns. Four holders of record hold the shares, and one United States record holder acting through the registrar holds 93.77% of them, so beneficial owners cannot be identified; the annual report incorporates its beneficial-ownership table by reference to a proxy statement that was not supplied. A holder crossing 30% of capital or voting rights must offer for all shares under the articles, and the senior notes carry a repurchase offer at 101% on a change of control, although the indenture definition of a change of control is not supplied.

Prices are set at metal cost plus a conversion margin, so earnings should follow margin and volume, but the business is concentrated by product and customer. Packaging rolled products are 44.63% of FY2025 revenue, the packaging and automotive rolled segment is 59.97% of external revenue, and the two largest customers are 21.25% of revenue, with the ten largest around 56%. Management says the largest aerospace contracts run for several years and general industrial contracts for a year or less, so contract visibility is strongest in the segment with the highest margin, 17.23% in FY2025 against 6.95% for packaging and automotive sheet.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 13, 93–94, 97; calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C11

The 2026 earnings step-up mixes base-case and temporary drivers, which matters because buybacks are paid from it. Revenue rose 25.61% in 9M 2026 while shipments fell 0.88%, so growth came from revenue per tonne, which the company ties to higher metal prices, not from volume, and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,074 million includes a non-cash metal price lag of USD 222 million, or 20.67%. Management credits automotive sheet shortages in North America, favourable scrap and strong recycling, and says its 2028 targets of Adjusted EBITDA of USD 900 million and free cash flow of USD 300 million, both before metal price lag, leave out the scrap environment and the 2026 shortage benefit; the 2026 guidance of USD 1,030 million to USD 1,060 million is above that EBITDA target, and guidance was raised at each of the three 2026 reports.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 33, 41; EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026-q1xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026-q2xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C9

Capital allocation favours shareholders inside a deleveraging track, a mixed pattern for creditors. Buybacks were USD 79 million in FY2024, USD 115 million in FY2025 and USD 78 million in 9M 2026, no dividend is paid, and a USD 300 million program runs to the end of 2028 with USD 257 million unused at September 30, 2026. In FY2024, with cash from operations of USD 301 million below net capital expenditure of USD 401 million, the company still repurchased shares and cash fell from USD 223 million to USD 141 million; in 9M 2026 free cash flow of USD 223 million covered buybacks 2.86x and the company repaid USD 106 million of long-term debt. The chief executive officer changed on January 1, 2026 through an internal succession, and the board extended the buyback authority in March 2026.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 49, 51, 64, 79, 123; 10-Q_2026-03-31_cstm-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 43; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C17

Behaviour toward creditors has been constructive in the documents supplied: refinancing into unsecured notes, longer liquidity facilities and a voluntary redemption. In August 2024 two 2032 note series replaced the 2026 notes, the French inventory facility was extended to December 2027 in February 2025, USD 100 million of the 2028 notes was redeemed on July 28, 2026, and on October 22, 2026 the Pan-U.S. ABL commitments rose from USD 550 million to USD 700 million with maturity moved to October 2031. No default, covenant waiver or exchange offer appears, and covenant compliance is stated at both balance sheet dates.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 65, 108–110; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cstm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 23; calculation C19; calculation C22

The guarantee and security structure is only partly visible, which limits the ownership and control map. The senior notes are unsecured obligations of the parent guaranteed by subsidiaries the filings do not name, while the US asset-based facility and the French inventory facility are secured on the assets of named operating subsidiaries; which entities guarantee the notes is not established, so the ranking of claims at the US borrowers cannot be drawn here.

Disclosure is adequate for monitoring, with one gap that matters, the proxy statement. The audited statements carry unqualified opinions with effective internal control over financial reporting, the company has filed as a United States domestic issuer since January 2026, and the auditor's one critical audit matter is the recoverability of deferred tax assets, USD 200 million net at year-end 2025. Board independence, executive pay and related-party dealings sit in the proxy statement and are not established.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a moderate risk level is the direction of travel: carrying debt fell from USD 1,944 million at December 2025 to USD 1,817 million at September 2026, leverage fell from 2.2x to 1.8x to 1.6x over the three 2026 quarters, free cash flow covered buybacks 2.86x, and no dividend, sponsor or creditor-adverse transaction appears. On behaviour alone the risk would be low.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026-q1xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026-q2xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C14; calculation C21

The view moves to low if the indentures and credit agreement, once supplied, show restricted-payment and debt capacity tight enough to keep distributions inside free cash flow, or if the board adopts a leverage ceiling below 2.5x. It moves to high if buybacks continue while cash from operations again fails to cover capital expenditure, as in FY2024, if leverage climbs toward the top of the 1.5x to 2.5x range while repurchases continue, or if a holder approaches the 30% bid threshold without a stated creditor protection.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 51, 64, 79; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C13
### Limitations

- Beneficial ownership and the votes attached to each share are not stated in the supplied filings, so the finding that no shareholder controls the company could be reversed if the proxy statement shows a holder near the 30% takeover-bid threshold or a group acting in concert.

- The note indentures, the credit agreement for the US asset-based facility and the guarantor list are not supplied, so the moderate risk level rests on observed behaviour and cannot be tied to the distribution, debt or lien capacity the documents allow; that capacity could move the risk level either way.

- Executive pay, board independence, related-party dealings and director holdings are in the proxy statement that the annual report incorporates by reference, so the finding that incentives follow relative share performance rests on the equity plan note alone.

- Customer names, contract expiry dates and the segment of each of the two largest customers are not stated, so the concentration finding rests on revenue shares and cannot show which renewals fall inside the life of the notes.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No acquisition, buyout, merger or sponsor transaction appears in the supplied filings for FY2025 or 2026 to date. The portfolio moved only at the edges: a USD 3 million purchase of a 51% controlling interest in Railtech Alu-Singen in August 2024 and the June 24, 2026 disposal of a 54% interest in Changchun Engley Automobile Parts Co. LTD for USD 2 million of cash net of cash disposed, so the credit is a standing operator rather than a deal.

The last new debt was issued in August 2024: USD 350 million of 2032 senior notes and EUR 300 million of 2032 senior notes, whose proceeds and cash redeemed the remaining 2026 notes. No exchange offer or amendment of the notes appears since, and debt has fallen: the July 28, 2026 redemption of USD 100 million cut the 2028 notes from USD 325 million to USD 225 million, and total debt at carrying value fell from USD 1,944 million at December 2025 to USD 1,817 million at September 2026.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 65, 109; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cstm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C19; calculation C21

Buybacks were USD 78 million in 9M 2026, and the board cancelled treasury shares on September 17, 2026 without any cash cost.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Constellium is an adequate and improving fundamental credit: leverage of 1.56x, no note maturity before June 2028 and USD 992 million of liquidity make near-term distress unlikely, but part of the 2026 earnings lift is temporary.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 38; calculation C2; calculation C9

The supports are qualified aerospace and packaging franchises with metal cost passed through and cash interest cover of 10.65x. The constraints are earnings that lean on one segment, working capital that absorbed USD 488 million in 9M 2026 and cash returned to shareholders. The primary downside path is a reversal of the packaging and automotive sheet margin, which a sensitivity puts at net leverage of about 1.89x, inside the 1.5x to 2.5x target range, ahead of USD 1,066 million of notes due in 2028 and 2029.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 15; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C19; calculation C8
### Key findings

Credit metrics are comfortable and maturities are distant, but the leverage level rests on a partly temporary earnings peak. Net debt at carrying value was USD 1,659 million at September 30, 2026, which is 1.56x last-twelve-month Segment Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,065 million against 2.53x at year-end 2025, and cash interest of USD 100 million is covered 10.65x. Every senior note carries a fixed coupon and none matures before June 2028, when USD 225 million falls due, followed by USD 841 million in 2029.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 79, 95; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C8

The 2026 earnings lift is concentrated and partly temporary, so today's leverage is a poor guide to normalised leverage. The packaging and automotive rolled segment produced 75.65% of the USD 345 million rise in last-twelve-month Segment Adjusted EBITDA over FY2025, the non-cash metal price lag is 23.05% of reported EBITDA, management says its 2028 targets leave out the favourable scrap environment and the 2026 automotive sheet shortage benefit, and guidance of USD 1,030 million to USD 1,060 million for 2026 implies fourth-quarter Segment Adjusted EBITDA of USD 178 million to USD 208 million against USD 213 million a year earlier.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026-q1xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C18; calculation C21; calculation C20; calculation C33

Cash conversion is the weakest financial dimension, because working capital absorbs the rise in metal prices. Free cash flow of USD 333 million over the last twelve months is 31.27% of Segment Adjusted EBITDA, and 24.72% in FY2025; working capital absorbed USD 488 million in 9M 2026 against USD 161 million a year earlier and cash taxes were USD 53 million against USD 17 million. Receivables of USD 417 million were factored off the balance sheet, and counting them as debt-like funding would put net leverage at 1.95x, against 3.13x at year-end 2025.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 14, 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 62, 79; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C10

The franchise is defensible but earns a thin margin outside aerospace. Cost of metal is 63.11% of FY2025 revenue, so conversion revenue is USD 3,117 million and Segment Adjusted EBITDA is 23.10% of it; the aerospace-led segment earned 17.23% on its revenue in FY2025 against 6.95% for packaging and automotive sheet and 4.56% for automotive structures. The two largest customers are 21.25% of revenue and the ten largest about 56%, so a single contract or one segment margin can move group earnings.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 93–94, 97; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C25

Financial policy is the main controllable risk. The board returned USD 78 million through buybacks in 9M 2026, covered 2.86x by free cash flow, a program of up to USD 300 million has USD 257 million unused, and the target range tops at 2.5x, which at constant earnings would allow USD 1,003.5 million of extra net debt, 60.49% of today's, before the top. There is no sponsor and no dividend, but the notes' distribution and debt limits are not supplied, so what the board is permitted to do is not established.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 43; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C7; calculation C23; calculation C32

Refinancing risk is moderate and rests on market access rather than liquidity. Cash and undrawn committed facilities of USD 813 million cover 76.27% of the USD 1,066 million of notes due in 2028 and 2029, so repayment needs refinancing or several years of free cash flow; the asset-based facility commitments rose to USD 700 million and its maturity moved to October 2031 after the balance sheet date. Quoted prices of the notes were 94.0% to 99.6% of nominal value at September 30, 2026 but fell by 1.2 percentage points to 4.3 percentage points since December 2025 despite stronger metrics, and the filings do not say why.

The claims structure is only partly visible, which limits conviction on ranking. Pension and other benefit obligations of USD 341 million sit outside debt, as do the factored receivables, the asset-based facility is secured on the assets of three US borrowers and the French inventory facility on French inventory, and the senior notes are guaranteed by subsidiaries that the filings do not name.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence that the credit is better than adequate is that the stress case stays inside the target range: if the packaging and automotive sheet margin returned to its FY2025 level, last-twelve-month Segment Adjusted EBITDA would fall by about USD 188 million to USD 877 million, net leverage would be 1.89x and cash interest cover 8.77x, with USD 992 million of liquidity and no note due before June 2028. The strongest evidence that it is weaker is that FY2024 showed negative free cash flow of USD 100 million while buybacks continued, and that the notes' quoted prices fell after the metrics improved.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 79, 110; calculation C19; calculation C17; calculation C4; calculation C24

The view moves toward strong if full-year free cash flow exceeds the USD 300 million the company guides and net debt keeps falling while buybacks stay below free cash flow. It moves toward weak if fourth-quarter Segment Adjusted EBITDA falls below the USD 178 million implied by guidance, if leverage on the company's definition rises above the 2.2x of March 2026, or if working capital absorbs another USD 488 million without reversing.

### Limitations

- The size of the temporary part of the 2026 earnings lift is not stated by the company, so the downside sensitivity assumes the packaging and automotive sheet margin returns to its FY2025 level and is an illustration, not a forecast; a smaller or larger reversal would move the stress leverage of 1.89x accordingly.

- The legal terms of the notes and the asset-based facility are not supplied, so the financial-policy view cannot say how much of the USD 1,003.5 million of leverage headroom the documents let the board use.

- Availability and borrowing-base terms of the asset-based facility after the October 22, 2026 amendment are not established, so the liquidity of USD 992 million and its 93.06% coverage of the 2028 and 2029 notes use pre-amendment availability and may be understated.

- No peer set, rating or traded yield is supplied, so the business profile cannot be compared with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector and the refinancing view rests on quoted prices at a single date.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strengths, in order of weight, are low leverage with strong cover, liquidity with distant maturities, a qualified-product franchise with metal pass-through, operating leverage that turned conversion revenue into earnings, and creditor-aligned behaviour. Net leverage of 1.56x and cash interest cover of 10.65x leave room to absorb a margin reversal; liquidity of USD 992 million and no note due before June 2028 remove near-term refinancing pressure; qualification processes and multi-year aerospace contracts support volumes; in 9M 2026 conversion revenue rose 20.75% while production costs rose 6.38%; and the company paid no dividend, redeemed USD 100 million of notes and extended its facilities.

The weaknesses, in order of weight, are earnings that are partly temporary, weak cash conversion, concentration, a shareholder-return and leverage policy that allows re-leveraging, and a refinancing wall in 2028 and 2029. The metal price lag is 23.05% of reported EBITDA and one segment produced 75.65% of the rise in Segment Adjusted EBITDA; free cash flow is 31.27% of Segment Adjusted EBITDA; the two largest customers are 21.25% of revenue; the target range tops at 2.5x with USD 257 million of buyback authority unused; and USD 1,066 million of notes fall due across 2028 and 2029.

### Company description

Constellium converts aluminium into specialty rolled and extruded products for aerospace, packaging, automotive and industrial customers, so its credit is that of a conversion business whose margin, not the metal price, drives cash flow. FY2025 revenue was USD 8,449 million across three segments, the group operated 23 manufacturing facilities at September 30, 2026, and the only portfolio changes in the period are a USD 3 million purchase of a controlling interest in 2024 and the 2026 disposal of a 54% interest for USD 2 million, so cash flow comes from operations, not from deals. Cash-flow visibility is strongest in aerospace, where the largest contracts are multi-year and the segment earned 17.23% in FY2025, and weakest in general industrial work, where contracts run a year or less.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 94, 96, 124; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cstm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C14; calculation C1; calculation C34
### Ownership and group structure

No sponsor or controlling shareholder appears in the supplied filings, so the board, not an owner, sets financial policy, and the parent is a French company listed on the NYSE whose US assets sit in a wholly owned US holding company. The senior notes are issued by the parent and guaranteed by unnamed subsidiaries, the asset-based facility is borrowed by three US operating companies and the inventory facility by two French ones, which layers the debt structure, and no dividend is paid while buybacks of USD 78 million were made in 9M 2026. A chief executive officer from within the company took over on January 1, 2026, and the board extended the buyback authority in March 2026, so the policy continued through the change.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 18, 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 43; calculation C32
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue growth in 2026 came from price, not volume, so revenue durability depends on conversion margins rather than on the metal price. Revenue rose 25.61% in 9M 2026 and revenue per tonne 26.73% while shipments fell 0.88%; aerospace and transportation shipments rose 19.48%, packaging and automotive sheet shipments fell 3.29% and automotive structures fell 2.58%. Prices are set at metal cost plus a conversion margin and customers face high switching costs from long qualification, which supports margins. Demand follows aircraft build rates and light vehicle production, which are cyclical, and beverage can demand, which the annual report calls relatively resilient in downturns and which is 44.63% of revenue through packaging rolled products; the United States takes 39.15% of revenue by destination and trade policy is a stated risk.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 11, 13, 23–24, 93; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C30; calculation C25
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are defended against metal prices by pass-through but remain exposed to volume, because the company says its capital-intensive operations generally have high fixed costs that it may not be able to cut quickly, and conversion costs are large against conversion revenue, although the filings give no fixed and variable split. Cost of metal is 63.11% of FY2025 revenue and passes through, production costs are 24.12% and other segment expenses 4.25%, so conversion costs take 76.90% of conversion revenue and, if every one were fixed, a 1% fall in conversion revenue would cut Segment Adjusted EBITDA by up to 4.33%. The same leverage worked upward in 9M 2026: conversion revenue rose 20.75% against production costs of 6.38%, lifting Segment Adjusted EBITDA 68.05%. A large part of energy needs is fixed-price, a majority of slabs are cast in-house, the ten largest metal suppliers supply about 49% of volumes, and the largest US labour agreements run to 2029 and 2030, which holds the cost base steady but limits flexibility if volumes fall.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 26, 56, 94, 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital spending is moderate but cash conversion is held down by working capital, taxes and interest, so earnings turn into free cash flow slowly. Net capital expenditure was 3.68% of FY2025 revenue and depreciation, amortization and impairment USD 351 million, with growth projects in recycling and casting that management can slow but whose split from maintenance is not stated. Free cash flow was negative USD 100 million in FY2024, USD 178 million in FY2025 and USD 333 million over the last twelve months, and in 9M 2026 working capital absorbed USD 488 million and cash taxes rose by USD 36 million, so only 31.27% of Segment Adjusted EBITDA reached free cash flow; the company's 2028 target is free cash flow of USD 300 million.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 96–97; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 39; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026-q2xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C26; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C33
### Competitive forces

Rivalry and buyer power are the likely reasons margins are thinner in packaging and automotive sheet than in aerospace, where qualification barriers protect them. The industry is competitive on quality, price, delivery and innovation, the packaging and automotive sheet segment earned 6.95% on revenue in FY2025 against 17.23% in aerospace-led products, and the two largest customers are 21.25% of revenue, which gives them negotiating weight, although the filings do not say which segment they buy from. New entrants face heavy capital needs and long customer qualification, substitutes such as steel, glass, plastics and composites compete in some uses, and supplier power is limited because most slabs are cast in-house and the ten largest metal suppliers supply about 49% of volumes.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 12–13, 94; calculation C14; calculation C25
### Macro, trade and currency factors

Trade policy and currency are material to credit, while social and technological factors are not primary credit drivers. The annual report names tariffs and shifting trade agreements as a risk to the supply chain and the industry, and the United States is 39.15% of revenue by destination, so a tariff change could reprice flows without any amount being stated; the euro notes are carried at USD 682 million of the USD 1,757 million of senior notes, so movements in the euro change reported debt without any cash flow while cash interest is fixed. Metal prices matter through the lag and working capital rather than through conversion margin.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24, 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C30; calculation C31
### Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats

The credit-relevant strengths are the qualified franchise, low leverage, liquidity and distant maturities, and the absence of a sponsor; the weaknesses are earnings that are partly temporary, weak cash conversion, concentration and a policy that permits leverage up to 2.5x. The opportunities that could improve credit quality are the company's stated 2028 targets, already expected two years early, and the extended asset-based facility; the threats are a reversal of the packaging and automotive sheet margin, a fall in metal prices that turns the lag negative, trade-policy changes and a debt-funded shareholder return.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026-q2xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C19; calculation C2
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale is strong, with USD 10,049 million of revenue over the last twelve months and 23 plants. Competitive advantage is average, strong in qualified aerospace and automotive products and weaker in packaging. Diversification is average: three segments, but one provides 59.97% of external revenue and the two largest customers 21.25%. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with capital spending of 3.68% of revenue and, by the company's own account, generally high fixed costs. Margin stability is average, with Segment Adjusted EBITDA margins of 8.52% in FY2025 and 10.60% over the last twelve months. Free cash flow stability is weak, from negative USD 100 million in FY2024 to USD 333 million over the last twelve months. Ability to refinance is average and improving, with notes quoted at 94.0% to 99.6% of nominal value and an extended facility. Liquidity is strong at USD 992 million with the first note due in June 2028. Financial policy and governance is average: no sponsor, no dividend and falling leverage, against buybacks and a target range that tops at 2.5x.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 38; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C1; calculation C26; calculation C4; calculation C25; calculation C24; calculation C9

The main supports are leverage, cover and liquidity; the main constraints are cash conversion and concentration; the trend is improving, with leverage down from 2.53x to 1.56x and net debt down USD 165 million in nine months; and the missing data are peer comparisons, ratings and the legal terms of the debt.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C22
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the credit is supported by an improved aerospace and defense environment, management guidance raised at each 2026 report, the asset-based facility extended to October 2031 and no note maturity before June 2028, while headwinds are a possible fading of the automotive sheet shortage and favourable scrap, a seasonally weak fourth quarter that guidance implies at USD 178 million to USD 208 million of Segment Adjusted EBITDA, and a metal price lag that reverses if prices fall. Over three to five years the company cites industry forecasts of 8.5% annual growth in aerospace rolled products in North America and Europe and 3.6% a year for aluminium rolled products to 2030, which support volumes, while the 2028 and 2029 notes of USD 1,066 million and trade policy are the main risks to refinancing and margins.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_cstm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 23–24; EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026-q1xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026-q2xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_a2026-q3xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C20; calculation C33; calculation C8; calculation C29; calculation C28
### Downside scenario

The primary downside is a normalisation of the packaging and automotive sheet margin that reaches creditors through leverage and refinancing, not through liquidity. The initiating condition is the end of the North American automotive sheet shortage and favourable scrap, which management says its 2028 targets exclude; the first operating break is a return of that segment's margin from 10.01% over the last twelve months to its FY2025 level of 6.95%, which removes about USD 188 million of Segment Adjusted EBITDA and takes it to USD 877 million. Net leverage would then be 1.89x and cash interest cover 8.77x, still inside the 1.5x to 2.5x range; a fall in metal prices would also turn the metal price lag negative in reported EBITDA but would release working capital, which absorbed USD 488 million in 9M 2026. Liquidity of USD 992 million and the absence of a note maturity before June 2028 mean that liquidity distress is not indicated; the board's levers are buybacks, which were USD 78 million in nine months, growth capital spending and factoring, and the observable trigger is fourth-quarter Segment Adjusted EBITDA below USD 178 million.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026-q1xearningspressre.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cstm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 38; calculation C17; calculation C19; calculation C5; calculation C9; calculation C20; calculation C7
### Overall credit view

Overall, Constellium presents an adequate business profile supported by qualified aerospace and automotive franchises, metal pass-through and no sponsor, but credit quality is constrained by thin margins in packaging and automotive sheet, customer and segment concentration, and a policy that permits leverage up to 2.5x. Cash-flow durability appears adequate, because free cash flow covered buybacks 2.86x in 9M 2026 but is only 31.27% of Segment Adjusted EBITDA over the last twelve months. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the leverage held through 2027, quoted note prices and the asset-based facility, ahead of USD 1,066 million of notes due in 2028 and 2029. The primary downside path is a reversal of the packaging and automotive sheet margin. How the business profile compares with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established, and a more definitive opinion would need the legal terms of the debt, a peer set and the availability of the asset-based facility after the amendment. The top risk is a margin reversal in packaging and automotive sheet.
